A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MM-MISLEADING and OMGuard. The complete 23-page v1 and 24-page v2, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support reliable comparison. Renumbered and duplicated material can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original detection and correction experiments, human annotation validation, ablations, attribution analyses, and a visual-intervention pilot.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a reasoning-model comparison and intermediate-supervision ablations in Table 1.

M1.justification: Section 5 retains the same interpretation-aware objective, supervision on rationale and judgment, generate-then-reason inference, and rationale-guided headline correction. The newly evaluated Up/Uc-supervised variants are ablation controls, not revisions to the proposed OMGuard procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same VisualNews-derived MM-MISLEADING coverage, ten topic categories, detection and correction tasks, editing modes, and image-driven scenarios. The text-only evaluation and 20-case visual-intervention pilot already appear in v1.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Qwen3-VL-235B-Thinking and two Up/Uc-supervised comparison variants using end-to-end and multi-stage inference. OMGuard (Label-Only) becomes FT Label-Only with unchanged scores. The correction comparator sets in Tables 2–3 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.4 changes the reported human detection audit from 200 randomly sampled instances to the full 1,000-instance test set; three annotators and 100 correction instances remain. Section 6.2 adds two inference settings for direct Up/Uc supervision. The main splits, training settings, metrics, and correction protocols remain unchanged. These are reported protocol changes, not independently verified reruns.

E4.justification: The new Section 6.2 ablations directly test supervising intermediate interpretations under end-to-end and multi-stage inference, supplementing the existing label-only and oracle-interpretation comparisons. The attribution chart and text-only table newly displayed in the main text reproduce existing appendix analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions use three annotators and report accuracy and Fleiss’ kappa. Neither introduces repeated-run information, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The revised kappa summary changes reported values, not the statistical reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds accuracies of 0.79 for Qwen3-VL-235B-Thinking and 0.87/0.78 for the two Up/Uc-supervised variants; existing scores remain unchanged. Section 4.4 raises its summary from kappa ≥0.72 and accuracy above 93% to ≥0.81 and above 94%, although the appendix retains the earlier values. Section 6.5 removes the claimed 0.13 accuracy decrease. The visual-replacement case label changes from Misleading in v1 Figure 9 to Non-Misleading in v2 Figure 10.

T1.justification: The task definitions, correction constraints, and Equations 1–4 remain unchanged. No new formal assumptions, mathematical derivations, theorems, or proofs are introduced; the added supervision and deployment arguments are empirical interpretations.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the benchmark, interpretation-aware detection, rationale-guided correction, 8B performance matching a 235B model, and findings about local omissions and visual limitations. The conclusion becomes more aspirational, but the platform-screening and newsroom-assistance roles remain explicitly claimed in the unchanged introduction.

C2.justification: Section 6.2 newly attributes direct interpretation supervision to conservative predictions and train–test mismatch, and argues that multi-stage inference offers better intervention and auditability despite end-to-end advantages. Much of the expanded context-repair discussion in Section 6.4 already existed in v1 Appendix A.4.2. The explicit limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a first-page footnote stating that data and code are available through a repository link absent from v1. This adds access information; repository contents are not established by the PDFs. Existing LoRA hyperparameters, training details, model-card entries, and appendix prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography and substantive positioning against fact-checking, intent analysis, framing, and clickbait research remain unchanged. Added inline model citations refer to works already cited in v1. DeceptionDecoder becomes DeceptionDecoded in Section 2 while referring to the same cited work.

P1.justification: The abstract, most experimental discussion in Sections 6.2–6.5, and conclusion undergo broad paragraph-level rewriting. v2 also expands the supervision and deployment discussion, adds acknowledgments, and edits affiliation and contact information. This is extensive narrative revision despite retaining the overall section hierarchy.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains three rows. v2 Figure 5 and Table 4 redisplay the attribution chart and text-only results already present in v1’s appendix; their appendix counterparts remain as Figure 6 and Table 6. Captions and pagination change, but the existing visual designs are largely retained.

improvement.justification: The additional supervision controls, reasoning-model baseline, access statement, and corrected case label improve evidential support and usability. However, v2 introduces an unresolved validation inconsistency: Section 4.4 claims expanded human evaluation with kappa ≥0.81 and accuracy above 94%, while Appendix Table 5 retains kappa values of 0.72–0.78 and detection accuracy of 0.93. This affects the credibility of the benchmark-quality evidence. The PDFs do not reconcile the discrepancy, so the benefits and reporting harm do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
